text.p: Salomon Brothers raised its 1997 and 1998 revenues and earnings per share estimates for Israel's Orbotech Ltd and said it was maintaining its strong buy recommendation.
Salomon raised its EPS estimate for 1997 to $1.96 from $1.79 per share and its 1998 EPS estimate to $2.28 from $2.00.
Orbotech is a maker of automated optical inspection (AOI) systems for printed circuit boards (PCBs).
"For 1997 we expect 22.5 percent revenues growth and a 27.7 percent increase in EPS. In 1998 sales are expected to increase 17.9 percent, while EPS will be up 16.1 percent," Salomon said in a report.
Salomon said that despite a recent jump in Orbotech stock it was still trading at 12 times the expected 1997 EPS and 10.3 times the 1998 EPS.

"Orbotech recently demonstrated its jointly developed (with east Germany-based Jenoptik) direct imaging systems which went very sussessfully. Commercial introduction of the system is expected in mid 1998," the report said.

"Orbotech is boosting its R&D expenses from 11 percent in 1995 and 11.5 percent in 1996 to an expected 12.5 percent in 1997. The company is gearing up in introducing a number of major new products, including shadow mask AOI, lead frame inspection system and direct imaging machines," the report said.
